title: Predictive Reservation & Canary Capacity Pipeline
creator: Evelyn Chen
description:
Goal: Build a predictive reservation intake and canary capacity pipeline that reduces time-to-provision, enforces throughput guarantees, and minimizes wasted reserved fleet by running a shadow allocation + canary traffic phase before committing long-term capacity. Scope covers UI intake changes, approval rules, autoscale policy templates, and capacity planner integrations.

Why: Customers frequently over-provision to avoid throttling; that increases cost and slows onboarding. A predictive shadow allocation that uses customer telemetry and a small canary window can validate throughput needs and the chosen autoscale profile before an SLA-backed reservation is created. This preserves our unit economics and reduces provisioning errors.

Key pieces to deliver: (1) Reservation intake form revamp with optional 'predictive mode' (samples historical traffic or runs a dry-run load test), (2) Canary capacity orchestration that spins up short-lived reserved pods connected to routing with traffic percentage control, (3) Approval guardrails that surface risk score, estimated burn, and throughput SLO checks to approvers, (4) Autoscale policy templates tuned for the customer's modeled distribution (latency P95 targets, batch size profiles), (5) Planner export to capacity forecasting and finance (monthly expected spend and commit window recommendations), and (6) Observability hooks: per-reservation telemetry, canary health dashboard, and rollback triggers.

Tradeoffs discussed: predictive mode requires sampling historical tokens and running a statistical model; this adds latency to onboarding and requires stored telemetry access (GDPR/PII considerations). Canary runs could increase short-term infra usage; we mitigate by limiting canary duration and weight. Approval complexity vs speed: we prioritize a single-click approve for low-risk customers and require multi-step approvals for high-risk/regulatory customers.

Out-of-scope (this ticket): full contract negotiation flows, billing system changes beyond forecast export, and support for air-gapped on-prem private deployments (will follow in a separate epic).
acceptance_criteria: UI: New reservation form has a 'Predictive mode' toggle with clear descriptions and links to the canary policy
Canary orchestration: System can schedule a short-lived reserved instance, route a configurable percentage of traffic for 4–72 hours, and collect SLO metrics
Autoscale templates: Provide at least three tuned autoscale policy templates (latency-focused, cost-focused, balanced) that can be selected during intake
Approval workflow: Approver sees risk score, estimated monthly burn, throughput SLO delta, and can approve/deny with an audit trail
Planner export: Reservation details and modeled spend exported to capacity planning dashboard and CSV for finance
Observability: Canary health dashboard created with per-reservation metrics, and automatic rollback rule triggers when P95 latency exceeds threshold or error rate > 1%
Telemetry and privacy: Predictive sampling respects customer privacy flags and only uses aggregated/retention-compliant telemetry
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Internal beta): predictive pipeline enabled for internal test accounts and 3 pilot customers (2 weeks). Phase 2 (External opt-in): open as an opt-in feature for new reservations with UI flag and product docs (4 weeks). Phase 3 (Default-on for low-risk tiers): enable by default for Standard tier customers with a 30-day notice and migration runbook (6 weeks). Post-rollout: monitor key metrics for 12 weeks and iterate.
